summary: Full e2e testing of the NEW media upload feature (logo/profile/header) — backend + frontend. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_media.py with 8 tests covering (1) 401 without token, (2) reject .txt, (3) reject video on logo field, (4) reject oversized image >5MB, (5) upload PNG logo returns {path,type:image} + public GET serves with image/* Content-Type, (6) upload MP4 on header field returns type:video, (7) unknown /api/files path → 404, (8) seed /api/public/clientes/studio-exemplo unaffected. All 8 pass. Full regression pytest run: 32/32 passed (test_auth 10, test_change_password 6, test_clientes 8, test_media 8). Frontend (Playwright, logged in): three MediaUpload widgets render in Novo cliente → Mídia section; wrong-type .txt → PT-BR toast 'Use imagem JPG, PNG ou WEBP.' and NO preview; oversized (6MB) → PT-BR toast 'Arquivo muito grande. Limite de 5 MB.'; valid PNG upload shows preview + filename + Substituir + Remover; Substituir replaces file; Remover clears preview back to choose state; created 'teste-midia' (Publicado) with logo+profile+header images uploaded; /c/teste-midia rendered with card-cover-image and card-profile-avatar both sourced from `${BACKEND_URL}/api/files/digital-cards-ia/uploads/...` and the card-logo chip visible (profile+logo both set); /c/studio-exemplo still renders DEFAULT_COVER (pexels) when no headerUrl — default fallback works. Cleanup: deleted teste-midia at end; DB left with only seed.
critical_code_review_comments: MediaUpload posts FormData to /api/media/upload but relies on the axios global Authorization header set at login — works, but there is no explicit retry/refresh on 401. If token expires mid-form the user will only see a generic toast; the parent handleSubmit does handle 401 → onLogout, but the upload itself doesn't.

GET /api/files/{path} loads the entire object into memory and returns Response(content=...). For 25MB videos this could pressure the API pod under concurrency — consider StreamingResponse and/or a redirect/presigned URL from the object storage.

MIME type on serve_file trusts record.get('content_type') stored at upload time (derived from extension). No X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header — low risk since ext is whitelisted, but worth adding.
backend/server.py is monolithic (~450 lines) and Admin.jsx is ~795 lines. Continue to prefer splitting: MediaUpload → own file, storage helpers → services/storage.py.

'Remover' clears the reference but does not attempt any delete; db.files record stays with is_deleted=False forever. Known limitation per requirements, but consider a soft-delete flag update so orphan tracking is possible.

Frontend MediaUpload derives filename from URL path (UUID.ext) so users only see a UUID, not the original filename they picked. Original filename is stored in db.files.original_filename — return it in the upload response and display it for better UX.
seed_data_creation: Created and DELETED test client 'teste-midia' during e2e. Uploaded objects (2 PNGs) remain unreferenced in object storage (no delete API available, per problem statement). DB left with only seed 'studio-exemplo'.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reuse /app/backend/tests/test_media.py. Note: tests need REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL exported (or defaults to production URL). MediaUpload data-testids: upload-{logo|profile|cover}-{choose|input|preview-image|preview-video|filename|replace|remove}. Card template testids: card-cover-image, card-cover-video, card-profile-avatar, card-logo. Frontend stores logoUrl/profileUrl/headerUrl as full `${API}/files/${path}` URLs and headerType as 'image'|'video'. Public page PublicCard maps cliente.headerType→coverVideo|cover accordingly.
